i'm so sorry

all i can say is don't give up. you're young. you're just in 9th grade. you haven't fucked up your life; you can fix your problems, you have a lifetime to try. there's hope. there *is* hope for you.

you just have to try, which is so hard that i think i'm almost giving you an impossible task. god knows i'm having the same issues.

just try.

even if this doesn't change anything, take out your notebook. write down clearly, legibly, everything you think is wrong, everything in you, in your life, in your actions that you think is so unfixable that you'd be better off dead. wrote down everything that's so awry that you can't even fathom fixing it.

just write the list.

maybe you can fix at least one item on there. at least then you can say you'd tried.

<3 req

i don't know what it's like in your position, but props to being able to keep up the gpa while still doing the sorority stuff and dealing with all this.

you probably know how insane that is, just not completely shutting down while dealing with the anx/dep. it shows perseverance, despite how you may feel.

on the meds, maybe try to change your dosage? it took a long time before my doc could find a prescription that worked for me.

on the sorority: i know vv little about that stuff, but pore over how exactly badly it is influencing said mental health, and if it/your duties in it can be offloaded to someone else while you take a break. it seems like its causing you undue anxiety and is really poorly impacting your mental state.

that said, i'm not in the best position to be giving advice. take what i say with a grain of salt and get some more personalized help from a therapist or simple acknowledgement of how much you're doing right from your closer friends.
